Arena result diagnosis (read-only), 2026-10-30
Candidate 12cc1c2fee782ff68604fa30f2f2c519a795474a. No new build, numerical run, profiler, or source change in this analysis. Sources: root's eight existing JSON samples in artifacts/overnight-arena-screen, candidate source, existing Release object disassembly.

Conclusion: stop this PMR direction and do not integrate. Heap allocation count was an intermediate metric. This prototype removed most upstream allocations but retained per-task ownership, interpretation, copies and graph work; its measured complete-time gain is absent. A broad compact-view redesign is not justified by these samples alone.

Recorded medians (four samples each; these separate medians do not sum into a synthetic run):
metric                          baseline       arena
whole score ms                  290.402716     291.070927
all-case prepare ms              21.113810      20.537854
case19 prepare ms                10.630367       9.826031
all-case execute ms             220.771020     223.370843
case compute-prep-execute ms     46.310698      42.897292
case19 compute-prep-execute ms   12.314949      11.051803
common remainder/finalize ms      1.014018       2.598020
case19 reported graph bytes      11135464       13813679
The four paired prepare differences change sign. The apparent lower case remainder may include reduced free costs, but also matrix allocation/initialization, resource probes, validation outside stage timers, and other work; it cannot be attributed to arena without the separate profile. Conversely common_finalize is NOT task-arena teardown: graphs die inside each case, while main.cpp794-805 releases matrices, executor and Program after the loop. Its consistent increase is an observation; allocator/free-layout interactions and noise remain hypotheses.

Why 58,903 to 192 global-new calls does not imply a comparable time gain:
1. Global-new count excludes PMR virtual dispatch. For q48's 19,600 numerical tasks, args/reads/writes are all nonempty: three PMR allocate calls per task remain, approximately58,800 calls. Existing Task copy ctor disassembly has indirect call *0x10(%rax) at offsets6726,67fa and the writes allocation path, followed by element copies. PMR vector destruction also invokes per-container deallocation (the resource body is a no-op), even though it no longer frees every array upstream. The benchmark still pays iteration and object destruction.
2. Task(const Task&,resource), metadata.cpp149-151, still deep-copies arguments and every Region; it first copies symbol. q48 has48 cholesky,1128 trsm,18424 madd from the source loops. The catalog yields77,176 numerical Regions and96,776 Task-symbol/Region-buffer copies. Their small names fit SSO on this tested libstdc++ build, so they never contributed to the global-new counter and all remain. Each Region remains64 bytes including a32-byte owning string. These are known remaining operations, not measured dominant costs.
3. PMR vector adds a resource pointer. Task grows104 to128 bytes (+23.1%); q48 descriptor capacity32768 costs786432 additional bytes. Reallocation still moves every descriptor, and main.cpp705 erases the leading copy task, moving every remaining Task again (equal allocators keep array storage stable, but fields still move). Pooled arrays improve placement but descriptor growth, payload copy bandwidth, pointer traversal, and strings remain. Reported graph budget rises24.1%; that includes conservative accounting and is not an RSS measurement.
4. The interpreter still recursively evaluates all argument expressions and all four geometry expressions per Region into BoundNode.scratch, then copies scratch into the retained Task. Scope/if/loop interpretation and existing integer semantics checks remain. Metadata.cpp1178-1187 is unchanged apart from container types. All graph geometry scans, divisions, buffer comparisons, dependency state and CSR building remain. These are not allocator work.
5. Array pooling touches only part of preparation and destruction. Baseline prepare totals about7.3% of the complete batch. Even eliminating all prepare could only remove that observed fraction before other side effects; eliminating malloc alone is necessarily much smaller, while execution remains about221ms. Whole-time samples have around10ms-scale dispersion.
6. The final allocator changed from geometric chunks (~8MiB final growth tail) to64KiB preferred chunks. Measured heap-request peak fell14,690,680 to11,153,848B and calls rose111 to192, but this only fixes slack; it does not eliminate copied objects or evaluation. TaskBatch name accounting remains a per-region traversal; the old implementation also estimated per-region costs, so do not pretend that traversal is uniquely new.

Views or compact descriptors would be a genuinely different mechanism, but are not currently authorized implementation work:
- A TaskView containing operator ID and spans/offsets into batch-owned arguments/Regions could replace three PMR vector objects, owning per-task symbol, and per-container teardown; buffer IDs could remove each Region's string. Stable chunks or offsets are required so growth does not dangle spans. A separate owning serial scratch/callback adapter preserves enumerate_program semantics and variable argument counts. All required symbol binding stays in counted Metadata/runtime ownership; do not invent hidden algorithm files.
- A direct bound-to-storage emitter would additionally write values into final arrays instead of scratch then deep-copy. This is the only suggested route that removes the copies above; merely replacing PMR with another allocator would keep them.
- However this changes shared Task APIs, source binding, graph accesses, runtime invocation and phase lifetime. Correctness and budget proofs are broader than this prototype. No source/profile evidence yet shows that copied-task/allocator work offers enough complete-time headroom to outweigh that change. Need the current diagnosis profile to distinguish interpretation, copying, allocation, graph, and residual costs first. Do not begin a redesign based only on allocation-count reduction or a single fastest sample.

Recommendation: keep this commit and evidence as a rejected structural experiment; prioritize the parent's buffer reuse candidate and current short profile. Reopen compact views only if the profile identifies material memcpy/string construction/Task destruction or PMR dispatch time that can actually be removed. No new source changes, no repeat threshold sweeps, no extra numerical runs from this agent.
